reviews.review_title: The recent DCA commission complaint…
reviews.review_text: The recent DCA commission complaint system is not working at Toyota Financials as I’ve been told by their Customer Relations call centre their records do not go far enough back. So even though I sent them the copy of the Agreement and other supporting evidence, they just send a boiler template response out. They have the temerity to say because they don’t hold records for those years, they say you cannot raise a complaint to the FCA which is a tactic to avoid responsibility for potential passed misdemeanours . I’ve raised a complaint of course with the FCA and encourage others to do so if you have been treated in the same shoddy way. No issue with Toyota cars but never use Toyota Financial services. They are very discourteous and rather dim in my opinion.

reviews.author: ME
reviews.review_title: One & done!
reviews.review_text: I am never signing a contract with them ever again. They are dishonest. Their dealers are good and knowledgable, but this is the worst company to ever finance your vehicle with. They are unprofessional over the phone, even hung up on me in my first attempt to get more information on this.There is a $2,500 discrepancy between my current contract balance and how much the vehicle is worth, yet they also said I could still owe almost $7,000 after surrender. That makes absolutely no sense. I also made a $5,000 down payment on the vehicle and have made all of my monthly payments on time.It feels misleading and unethical for a financial institution to quote inflated “vehicle values” that don’t reflect what they actually plan to sell the car for. Instead of providing a clear explanation or transparent numbers, I was given confusing and contradictory information.Honesty and transparency matter. UNFORTUNATELY, I didn’t experience either here. Believe the reviews, and think twice before signing your life away.

reviews.review_text: I recently upgraded my Toyota Yaris to a C-HR at FRF Toyota Swansea.As I didn’t have my V5C logbook at the time, I was told I had to pay a £250 deposit until I provided one. I expected far better customer service from a Toyota dealership.

reviews.author: OL
reviews.review_title: Credit damage despite loyalty and clean history
reviews.review_text: I have been a loyal Toyota Finance customer for over 6 years with a perfect payment history — not a single missed or late payment. Unfortunately, my recent experience has been deeply disappointing and financially damaging.Due to a claim placed by Toyota Insurance (not by me), I was forced to return my vehicle. I did not initiate this claim, yet it impacted my insurance policy, and as a result, I returned the vehicle under a voluntary agreement. Despite this, Toyota Finance reported my account as delinquent to credit agencies — even after offering me a payment arrangement for the remaining balance.This is unfair and potentially unlawful under several consumer protection standards, including:🔹 The Consumer Credit Act 1974 (UK) / Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA – USA): These laws require accurate and fair reporting of consumer credit behavior. Reporting a delinquency while simultaneously offering a payment plan and knowing the customer has not defaulted in good faith may constitute unfair or inaccurate reporting.🔹 The Principles of Treating Customers Fairly (FCA – UK): Lenders must act in the best interest of the customer and treat them with fairness, particularly those in vulnerable or unexpected situations.As a result of this negative mark on my credit file, I have been declined finance by another vehicle dealer, even though the situation was not due to financial irresponsibility but rather an insurance-related technicality entirely out of my control. This damage is not only unjust — it is long-lasting.I am extremely disappointed that Toyota Finance, despite my long-standing, spotless history, chose to report my account in a way that severely impacts my ability to access credit. I am now pursuing options to escalate this through:A formal complaint to Toyota FinanceRaising a dispute with the credit reference agenciesSubmitting a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service (UK) or the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (USA)Seeking legal advice for defamation of creditLoyal customers deserve better — especially those who have upheld every part of their agreement. I urge Toyota Finance to reconsider their reporting decision and correct this unjust entry on my credit file.

reviews.review_title: When you call

reviews.author: LL
reviews.review_title: DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY!
reviews.review_text: DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY!direct debts have been rejected/cancelled on their end and for over a year i have had to log on to the website and pay manually. each time i try and set it up, they cancel it without any reason or acknowledgment.in January, i paid my installment manually but they said a week later i owed them a further £53. i stupidly paid this but still to this day believe they were wrong,  just didnt have the energy to go back and forth.2 weeks later before my next payment was due, i receive a message saying i am over £300 in arrears. this is more than 2 months worth of payments. somehow, miraculously  in the space of 2 weeks of being up to date i am now over 2 payments behind.i have spoken to a collections advisor and asked for them to provide me proof of what i owe and from where. he said its a tricky one to do and i just need to 'trust him'.sorry, but what idiot is going to just hand over a load of money without any valid reason or proof. they are con artists.i have raised an official complaint last month, chased up the complaint with another email and i am still yet to hear anything. no direct debit set up and now they have shut down my online portal to not allow me to see my balance or make any payments. all of this is affecting my mental health as well as my credit score!!!!!worst decision i ever made.

reviews.author: Camille Brooks
reviews.review_title: Unacceptable Customer Service
reviews.review_text: I am extremely disappointed with the service I received from Toyota Financial Services. I called to request payoff information with the intention of trading in my current Toyota for a new one, as I truly love my Toyota vehicle. Unfortunately, my experience was far from what I expected.I spoke with a representative named Darwin (ID #IGCW), and he was not only unhelpful but downright rude. He ended the call abruptly by hanging up on me, leaving me without the information I needed. This level of customer service is completely unacceptable, especially when I’m a loyal Toyota customer hoping to continue doing business with the company.If customer service is important to you, I would strongly urge you to reconsider before choosing Toyota Financial Services. Based on my experience, I will be looking elsewhere for my next vehicle purchase.Disappointed and frustrated

reviews.author: CB
reviews.review_title: Lease Buyout Nightmare
reviews.review_text: I have leased vehicles through Toyota/Lexus Financial Services for many decades, with no issues. They even gave me lease extensions during the COVID years, when I was reluctant to go car shopping--or anywhere!But I am writing about my current experience.My lease is up at the end of this month. I decided to buy the car, since leasing a new vehicle (same model, different year) would have cost nearly twice what I am currently paying--BEFORE the tariffs that are making America great and certain corporations and individuals wealthier--go into effect.  So I phoned Toyota Financial to get the buyout information and documents.First of all, the company is technologically in the dark ages. Maybe even prehistoric.Although they were able (at my insistence) to send me he paperwork I needed via email, I had to print, complete, and return the documents to them (by mail) along with a paper check for the buyout amount plus sales tax. They even sent me a form for California residents, though I live 3,000 miles from California.They are incapable or doing electronic bank transfers, accepting credit cards, etc. Just paper checks. (Fortunately, I still have a checkbook, but the last time I used it was 2007.)So, I did what I was supposed to do, and sent the documents and check to Toyota via Priority Mail.  Tracking indicated that it was delivered on 3/26.Eight days later, my bank records showed that the check still had not been cashed. I phoned the company, went through their annoying telephone menu, and after about 10 minutes, I got a "human" (and I use that word loosely) on the line. He was an arrogant and extremely unhelpful young man, whose only response to my inquiry about why my check had not been deposited was, "It takes 10 days for processing," and it was only day 8.  I imagine that for them, processing means opening the mail, then sending an employee to the bank to make deposits, since they are incapable of conducting business electronically.The rep could not or would not tell me how long it would take, once my documents were "processed, "for the bill of sale and title to be sent to me.And how would it be sent? By US mail, of course, which lately, in my experience, has been taking up to a full month for cards and letters to be delivered. They would not send my documents by Priority Mail. My only alternative was to pay an exorbitant fee for FedEx overnight service.It is now 4/5 or 11 days since Toyota received my check, and it still has not been deposited.To compound the absurd wait, Toyota will not transfer the existing vehicle registration to me, which means that I have to go to DMV and wait for hours to register the car in my name.  But wait....They have no way to inform me when the documents I need to register the car have been "processed" and mailed. The current registration, in the name of Toyota, is due in 3 weeks. In all likelihood, I will have to pay to renew the existing Toyota registration, then go to DMV and pay AGAIN to obtain new registration in my name.This is possibly the WORST customer service I have ever received in my life.I asked the arrogant customer disservice representative if he enjoyed working for a company that made things as difficult as possible for their clients, and he merely repeated that "processing takes 10 days."One more thing. I had been told a while ago that I could do the buyout through the dealership from which I had leased it. I thought that would simplify things and had intended to do that. However, when I met with someone at the dealership, I was informed that I would have to pay $900 in fees and various service charges for them to do the transaction--plus title and registration fees to the State. And they also would accept only cash or a paper check. Thanks, but no thanks.All I can say is, that if I ever want to lease a Toyota/Lexus vehicle again, it will be through a bank, NOT Toyota Financial Disservices.

reviews.author: TS
reviews.review_title: Shame on you Toyota Financial Services
reviews.review_text: I have 12 payments left on my loan, all my payments have been on time and on most occasions even early! So when my husband was diagnosed with cancer I immediately called TFS to ask for help, all I wanted to do was take my next two payments and add them to the end of my loan. I was approved for this immediately and the gentlemen I spoke with (on 2/24/25) couldn’t have been nicer or more caring. Done, I had two months where I could concentrate on paying my husbands medical bills and not have to worry about scraping together a car payment.Fast forward to today (3/28/25) when I receive a letter in the mail saying I am behind on my car payments AND I am being charged late fees!When I called the customer service number I was told they never received the necessary paperwork I HAD MAILED to them. What?!Soooo….no phone call to me? They know WHY I was asking for deferred payments, they asked me why when I initially called….so why no follow up about not receiving the paperwork?! Just a you owe this amount letter in the mail??I WILL NEVER buy a Toyota OR finance ANY vehicle through Toyota Financial Services ever again. They have lost a customer, actual, more than a few customers now that I posted my story all over social media to family and friends.I asked for help….instead I was ignored and then demanded money from. If this effects my credit score, and I will check, they better be prepared, because I will be holding them responsible.Beware people. Beware.

reviews.author: MO
reviews.review_title: If I could give this company zero Stars…
reviews.review_text: If I could give this company zero Stars I would. Payments taking at least a week to come out of my account and that's if I still have the money by the time that week is up because I live paycheck to paycheck and all of a sudden I think my bill is paid because it's been a week and then two weeks after my payment was due I finally get the email saying that the payment failed. Then I get to hope that I can afford to keep that money in my account for that week until they take it out otherwise, 2 more weeks go by before they notify you and text thing you know your ANOTHER month behind. reviews.review_text: I gave my car back and agreed with Toyota/Redline Finance. I recently received a letter from Toyota/Redline Finance regarding arrears on my account. Whatever you do, avoid these quacks.

reviews.review_title: This is a less than zero stars…
reviews.review_text: This is a less than zero stars situation.Toyota Financial Services (UK) are unresponsive, muddled and in complete disarray. It’s more or less impossible to get through on the telephone and their opening hours are not useful if you have a job - ringing in your lunch break isn’t enough time to get through.Email is even worse. Response times very long or not at all.TFS have managed to put the new finance agreement for a car I used to own annd part exchanged  onto my app.They have also altered the direct debit and taken payments for a car I don’t own anymore. I’ve cancelled the direct debit and I am paying the correct agreement via debit card while they ‘investigate’Meanwhile, the current owner of my previous car is defaulting (through no fault of their own)They send half replies, replies that don’t answer the questions asked and despite multiple queries about why I have someone else’s finance agreement on my app- they won’t reply to this- or remove the agreement.I finally gave up with ‘customer support’ after two weeks and emailed complaints. 4 days later I received a cut and paste response informing me that they would investigate and I would hear back ‘within 8 weeks’They then took a direct debit payment for an agreement that isn’t mine.I emailed customer experience detailing the horrible experience I had had so far. Guess what. It’s 4 days later and I’ve not even had an acknowledgement.Toyota cars are excellent. Toyota Financial Services is not. I’ve been a loyal Toyota owner and I change my car very frequently. I think my next step will be to get my supplying dealer involved but I shouldn’t need to be using up all this time and energy trying to sort out their admin error 🤷‍♀️

reviews.author: Dean Cane
reviews.review_title: Toyota Financial Services Mafia
reviews.review_text: I attempted to pay off my car loan with Toyota Financial Services (TFS) on August 13, 2024, by sending in a check. However, at the beginning of September, I received a notification that I was behind on a loan payment. Concerned, I contacted Toyota Financial to inquire about the situation. During my call, a representative from TFS informed me that they had not received my check and that I needed to make a payment to avoid late fees.Initially, Toyota had informed me that they received the check, had processed my loan to a zero balance, and had released the lien on the title. However, about 30-40 days later (around September 23), after the check had been sent, they reestablished the loan and indicated that the payoff was not processed as originally agreed. Following this, I cancelled the check.M&T Bank has documented evidence showing that the payment was made. It appears that there was internal miscommunication at Toyota Financial, as one department reported receiving the payment while another did not. I have made multiple attempts to reach out to Toyota's customer service through my loan account, but their response was dismissive, only stating that I was behind on my payments. They provided no further assistance or clarification.After this incident, I received the free and clear title to the car about two weeks later, but despite this, I continued to face issues when trying to resolve the situation. I called Toyota multiple times, trying to pay off the loan for the original amount I had sent in August, minus the most recent payments. However, Toyota informed me that the payoff amount had increased and they would need to seek approval to potentially forgive the additional interest. This response was unacceptable to me, as there was no guarantee they would do so, and I felt Toyota was mishandling the situation. Their actions were damaging my credit, and I lost confidence in Toyota Financial Services' ability to resolve the issue fairly and competently.On December 13, I attempted to reach out again, but once again, I was met with unreasonable responses. TFS insisted that I allow the check to go through their process, which could take several months. reviews.author: ES
reviews.review_title: Credit rating trashed by their error and they won't help
reviews.review_text: TFS neglected to use the new bank account information I submitted on their website on August 9, 2024, for recurring payments, which I’ve made without a “miss” since I acquired the car from Toyota in 2018.   Nor did the website indicate that a new recurring instruction was necessary when I changed the bank account.  Toyota failed to make the debits from the new bank account, and then declared me delinquent!I only learned of the problem when I saw that my FICO score dropped by 117 points on October 11th, 2024, via Experian.The amount in arrears was paid the day I was made aware via the credit report downgrade (i.e. October 11, 2024) and the recurring order is in place.  I have screenshots supporting all of the foregoing.I requested that TFS amend my status with the credit reporting agencies – Experian, Equifax and Transunion – to not delinquent - and do what TFS can towards restoring my prior credit standing.  I did this directly with TFS, and then through the auto dealer when I saw they wouldn't budge.  They were helpful and escalated with their contact at TFS.  However, TFS still refuses to acknowledge their error, as reflected in the form letter I received dated November 18 2024.  It matches exactly the one they sent me after I contacted them directly, dated they (that's how I see it), and I'm still stuck with a large hit to my credit rating.

reviews.author: TI
reviews.review_title: I would give -10 if this was…
reviews.review_text: I would give -10 if this was possible... Run away from them . The biggest mistake you could do is to get in any kind of contact with them . So we bought a car in April 2024 on finance with them . Car comes up faulty in less than 30 days , we returned to dealer multiple times before contacting Toyota and file a formal complaint with them . No response  from Toyota  that complaint was received.  So we called them . Apparently emails send to yahoo mail bounced back . Ok could happen.  So I change the email to Gmail. Or atleast I taught so . 3 days later I found out that email hasn't been changed ( so another 1 hour on phone ) ,after 4 long phone calls , million times been transferred  from one person to another . FINALLY I get conformation that my complaint was actually received.  So far so good , but unfortunately  this is just the beginning. So i suppose to get response from Toyota financial 4-8 weeks after I placed the complaint. Fine , 4 weeks pass so I called them to see if there is any update on the case . So after 45 min on phone transfered between 4 different operators I ve been promised that person who is dealing with my case will contact either me or my wife on next day . Happy days ... but a week no word from them , so i called them again , same empty promise again .Now 2 weeks later I decided  to again waist some of my time and call them again . Apparently I will someday get a call from them . Meanwhile I'm paying for scrap car parked in my driveway that I neither can use or return . And also I have been assured today from the person on the phone that their investigation is that car faulty  or not  will be done without even car to be seen by independent service . So I'm assuming person dealing with my claim have crystal ball that will tell him/her is car faulty or not . I can't hide my disappointment from this company.  It's just a joke .

reviews.author: EP
reviews.review_title: I am extremely disappointed with the…
reviews.review_text: I am extremely disappointed with the service I received from Toyota Financial Services. I sold my car to Carfax on July 30th, and they promptly sent the check for the remaining balance to Toyota. However, Toyota Financial did not process the payment until three months later. This unreasonable delay resulted in Toyota falsely reporting missed payments and sending my account to collections.Despite the fact that the payment was sent on time, my credit score took a significant hit due to Toyota’s incompetence. Trying to resolve the situation has been a nightmare, with unhelpful customer service and no accountability for their mistakes.I expected better from Toyota, but this experience has completely shattered my trust in their financial services. Be cautious if you're considering financing through them—this could happen to you too.

reviews.author: RO
reviews.review_title: STAY AWAY FROM THIS COMPANY
reviews.review_text: Becoming familiar with Toyota Financial Services has been the worst experience of my life, even eclipsing having a fractured skull and brain haemorrage since I had the misfortune of signing a finance agreement with this shower. Got a 4 year old car that developed a fault after 2 weeks and sent it back and the problem was bodged and the exact same fault reappeared more than 6 months later (emissions fault - countdown to impossible to start from 700 miles). Made a complaint to TFS and they completely ignored all of my correspondence and then sent their final response after exactly 8 weeks to extend the hardship for as long as possible. Their final response then said that the car hadn't been seen since it was purchased even though I provided them with the evidence of the first trip to the garage, the details of the fault and the invoice. I am currently waiting on the investigation of the Financial Ombudsman to conclude but I have had a completely useless car outside for 5 months now that I'm still paying for. I wish I had seen this page before I entered the agreement. This company should be prosecuted. They are an absolute disgrace. STAY AWAY!

reviews.author: KN
reviews.review_title: Don’t buy from Schottenkirk Toyota in ANY state!
reviews.review_text: Purchased a 2024 Toyota Highlander from Schottenkirk Toyota of Weatherford, TX. Purchased on June 26. Vehicle was not in stock but was allocated to this dealer. Was on a boat coming to Houston, TX. Told we could pick it up in 3/4 days. Finally was able to pick the vehicle up July, 14.  My payment was set for August 11. Had to completely do the application and all paperwork over again. Got a call from the dealer that Toyota Financial was not honoring the 4.75% rate because the new dates on the contact was in July. Had to come back a third time and do a paper application and contract package after we had been driving the vehicle a week. Here it is August 8 and I still have not heard from Toyota Financial and my payment is due 8/11.  Dealer says don’t worry, it’s only accumulated interest since June 26 with no ability to pay principle only to get the per payment interest rate down lower and pay off early. Bob Schottenkirk’s “customer first” vision has been replaced with the vision of the customer over a barrel being greased up for the screwing. Stay away from any Schottenkirk Toyota dealer and by all means never finance with Toyota Financial. If this ever gets straightened out I’m refinancing through a Navy Credit Union.

I am now stuck with my vehicle for another year and I will never ever be using this company again.

reviews.author: MA
reviews.review_title: Think carefully
reviews.review_text: Hi all,I took out an agreement with Toyota Finance in 2021. I love the car! I am certain I was told that I could pay off any sums I wanted after a set period and this would affect the final amount I owed. I recently tried to do this to discover this is not the case. The end sum stays the same even if you pay money in the interim. All paying early does is shorten the agreement or decrease the monthly payments.For older people, this kind of agreement does not work. So I would recommend anyone over 55 thinks carefully about taking out an agreement with these people.

reviews.review_title: Paid off Loan and still no Lien Release Document
reviews.review_text: I paid off my vehicle in July 2023.....almost 12 weeks later I still do NOT have the lien release document needed to physically take into the DMV to obtain the title for my vehicle.  I called multiple times to inquire and I was told they are working on it and I should receive it in the mail soon. I called twice and it was only documented I called once about my title. The woman I spoke to the 3rd time today argued with me and then hung up on me.Also beware of the GAP insurance because they lied to me at the dealership at Elk Grove Toyota in California and told me once I paid down my loan and the value of my car was more than what I owed I could remove the GAP insurance.  This is a true statement except it DOESN'T lower your payment because they bundle the GAP insurance with the car loan and it is a fixed payment.  When I called Toyota the man I spoke to in the GAP insurance department told me it happens ALL THE TIME! They used tricky wording to deceive me into believing I could lower my monthly payment by removing the GAP insurance. I was so angry with Toyota when I found out they tricked me. Rotten Scammers!!!!

reviews.author: Red Green
reviews.review_title: Toyota Financial Service Terrible
reviews.review_text: Toyota Financial Service charges higher than usual fees and interest rate. I suggest using a local bank or credit union. I have financed 3 vehicles with them and have owned 4 Toyota trucks. I have good credit and a perfect payment record on my current vehicle to date. Toyota sells to American but never the less, they offshore their services and fail to employ American inside the U.S. to serve the needs of United States residents for all their services. In the past, I have had to deal with them when I was unemployed and had a good relationship with them. Despite having a perfect payment record currently, I find the online and telephone customer services to be differcult to use and fustrating for a older person. Their customer service persons can be hard to understand and down right rude, sometimes. Toyota, generally makes a good vehile at a fair price. Their dealers are sometimes unethical, I have found in the past. I again, suggest dealing with a local bank or credit union that you do business with regularly to  to finance your major purchase. If you need to speak to a person, you can go right to the branch and see them face to face. You will be treated better as a person and get a better rate!

reviews.review_title: I have had two financial agreements…
reviews.review_text: I have had two financial agreements with this company over the past four years. Two running at the same time. I had nio response to the email, I then over the course of a few days, sent my complaint to two further different email addresses for Toyota Financial Services. reviews.author: PC
reviews.review_title: I had to make 4 different calls to them…
reviews.review_text: I had to make 4 different calls to them this afternoon to get connected with a representative. Almost impossible to get away from the bot to get a person. I wanted to get a payoff letter from TFS so my bank can send them the pay off balance of my loan. Why I could not do this online through my TFS account is a mystery to me. The rep told me it would take 3 days to e mail the payoff info to my banker and that they had to mail me an authorization letter to sign and give to my bank. They could not e mail me the form only mail it and it would take 7 to 10 days. After signing it I could e mail it to my banker as it had to go along with the bank's payoff. It all appears to me to be Toyota's plan to get as much interest as they can before I can payoff the balance. Unbelievable that TFS does not have a better IT set up as all of this should be able to be done on line.

Been on hold for near 30 minutes, absolutely disgraceful way to run a company!

reviews.author: Tammy Alicia Lewis
reviews.review_title: I’m suing these people for what their…
reviews.review_text: I’m suing these people for what their putting my son through with their stupid so-called  GAP insurance. I spoke with an attorney today about it. He informed me that in the height of Covid when all these financial institutions were so “so called” gracious in letting people defer payments to so-call help them in their time of need they neglect to tell the customer the fine print on what might happen on the back end of things! My son had a 2021 Toyota Supra his dream car that he got in a wreck and they totaled it out. He had GAP insurance. Now 5 months later Toyota financial sends him a letter saying he owes them $990 for a deferred payment he didn’t even ask for. They offered to do it for him. NOT telling him if something happened to his car that GAP wouldn’t cover any deferred payments!! He’s trying to buy another car now but can’t because he has this hanging over him! Toyota can either wipe this clean off his account with them or buy him another car free and clear by the time my lawyer is done with them!! Shame on you Toyota financial GAP for doing these kids this way especially during a time when we’re the most vulnerable!! 🤬🤬☹️🤨🤨

reviews.author: Mark Baird
reviews.review_title: Toyota Financial doesn't release titles
reviews.review_text: If you ask the rep at Toyota financial, they will tell you that it is their policy to release titles after a lien is paid off. Our family has owned a lot of Toyotas and I can say that has never happened once. You have to contact Toyota Financial and that is process is always awful. You can have them call you back rather than wait on hold but what I got out of that was a call from the company robot with no one on the other end, just silence. You can call back and stay on hold and listen to an awful twangy bit of country pop that repeats several times a minute and will burn itself into your brain. Finally talk to a human and he will tell you whatever he feels is right, you follow the steps and wait for the doc to arrive and after several weeks you call back and after ten minutes of more of that awful song designed to make you hang up, you get informed that you were misinformed and you need to fax different docs, which no one felt any obligation to inform you of until you personally go through the aggravation of calling back. Even worse, they insist of having the docs arrive by fax. Anyone still have a working fax machine? It will cost me about $40 to fax the docs that they didn't know they wanted until they rejected what they first asked for. My case was closed until I called back. What do we make of a company that markets itself for its advanced tech and hasn't figured out email by 2022? We've had to deal with this four times in the last 3 years. It's enough to make me think twice about ever signing up for this treatment by buying Toyota ever again.

Even worse, they insist of having the docs arrive by fax. Anyone still have a working fax machine? What do we make of a company that markets itself for its advanced tech and hasn't figured out email by 2022? We've had to deal with this four times in the last 3 years. It's enough to make me think twice about ever signing up for this treatment by buying Toyota ever again.

reviews.review_title: Due to covid 19 pandemic my work hours…
reviews.review_text: Due to covid 19 pandemic my work hours were cut as well as my fiancé loosing her job and the arrival of our newborn son has gotten really tight. Toyota deferred a few payments and things slowly went back to normal and I have never been late or missed a payment since. I asked again for the same courtesy after the truck had grave mechanical issues just hitting the 100k mark. Now with the covid resurgence and no longer being paid for the days we miss, money has got tight. I was denied, I have spoken with multiple friends in the same predicament and have been given courtesy by other lenders. I feel Toyota does not stand by it’s products and does not care about its customers, only the paycheck. My families Christmas was shot this year and just trying to pay my bills is getting tough. My company a large commercial mechanical contractor in NJ will discontinue use of Toyota Tundra vehicles and be going with Ford now. I am a combat veteran and hard working American and this will be my last Toyota vehicle. I just want others to know about Toyota financials incompassion and warn you before you spend 60k on their product like I did.

reviews.review_text: March 19, 2025 REMOVED BBB Review This is in response to the review submitted by REMOVED , against Toyota Motor Credit Corporation (TMCC), regarding the request to remove a vehicle from the REMOVED . First and foremost, TFS would like to thank Mr. REMOVED for the service he provided to our country. We strongly and proudly support the men and women in our military along with the veterans who have previously served. We recognize the sacrifice our military, veterans, and their families have endured. Our records indicate on February 25, 2025, our REMOVED received a fax document requesting the removal of the vehicle. However, the submitted documents contained incorrect lienholder information and lacked the commanding officers name contact details, delaying approval. Following continued communication with Toyota REMOVED we received the correct vehicle insurance verification on March 03, 2025. As of the date of this response, the vehicle removal request has been approved, and the consent form has been emailed to the address on file. reviews.review_text: Thank you for your response dated February 21, 2025.Your reply attempts to redirect accountability by stating that Toyota Financial Services (TFS) is merely an indirect lender and not responsible for dealership actions. However, this does not address the core concern: the alleged unauthorized access and use of customers trust or Social Security related accounts to fund vehicle purchases, while simultaneously charging interest and monthly payments effectively resulting in double payment.Whether directly or through third-party dealers, REMOVED assumes responsibility when it accepts assignment of contracts and proceeds to collect payments from consumers. As the assignee and servicing entity, TFS is obligated to ensure transparency and lawful processing of funds. Simply citing compliance with general applicable laws does not negate potential wrongdoing or shield your institution from scrutiny.The question remains:If vehicles are paid in full through access to consumer trust accounts, why are customers then obligated to make loan payments and interest payments as if the vehicle has not already been paid for?Your response also does not address the demand for a complete accounting of how any funds related to consumer trust or Social Security-based accounts are accessed, allocated, or recorded in your system.This is a call for transparency and accountability not a deflection of responsibility.TFS may wish to reconsider its approach, as growing numbers of consumers are becoming aware of these financial practices and are prepared to take legal and public actions to seek restitution, full disclosure, and justice.The request for cease and desist still stands.

reviews.review_text: February 17, 2023 REMOVED BBB Review This is in response to the review submitted by REMOVED against Toyota Motor Credit Corporation (TMCC) regarding her concerns with a double payment made toward her Toyota Financial Services (TFS). First and foremost, we regret to learn of her financial hardship, secondly, we would like to extend our sincerest apologies for any frustration Mrs. REMOVED endured when contacting our Customer Experience Center to discuss her account's remitted payments. Our records reflect on January 21, 2023, Mrs. REMOVED authorized a one-time payment via the Toyota owners App to deduct $455.14 using with bank account number ending with REMOVED . Also on the same day, with nine hours difference, she scheduled an additional payment via the Toyota's website (TFS) for the same amount $455.14. After conducting a thorough investigation, TFS received two payments that were both authorized by Mrs. REMOVED . We recognize that this was not her intention and have taken steps to expedite the application of the funds as mentioned below. Please be advised, our customer has the option to remit their monthly payments via TFS website of their Toyota owners App whichever they prefer. On January 25, 2023, Mrs. REMOVED contacted our Customer Care Center regarding her additional payment of $455.14, and per the conversation, she was advised a paper check will be mailed to her at the system address on file. It is important to understand that website payments are considered non-certified funds and may result in an appropriate hold for 7-10 business days before a refund is processed. On January 31, 2023, check number REMOVED was mailed for the over payment to the system address on file. Please be advised, we assume all refunds checks are received by our customer, unless we are notified otherwise by our customer. Our records reflect on February 17, 2023, our Corporate Customer Service attempted contacted Mrs. REMOVED , but with no success.
